app.name: Trees vs Breath
app.tagline: Test a street's trees before anyone plants them.
theme.label: Theme
footer.simulated: Every model number in this app is simulated and tagged as such.
start.question: Plant a tree — cooler street or dirtier air?
start.lede: In a narrow Hong Kong street, a tree can shade the pavement and still make the air at your nose dirtier. Test the street before anyone plants.
start.method: AI proposes, physics verifies, the wind tunnel judges.
start.illustration: Illustration of an example street with assumed dimensions. The live simulation arrives in phase 1.
section.title: Cross-section of a street canyon
street.title: Street
street.intro: Three real Hong Kong streets, measured from Lands Department building and road data. Open one in Design to test trees and hedges in it.
design.title: Design
design.intro: Wind blows across a street from the left, and traffic fumes rise from four lanes. Change the street's shape, add trees or a hedge, and watch where the fumes go.
tradeOff.title: Trade-off
tradeOff.intro: Every design the AI swept, plotted as heat against fumes. A design on the frontier cannot get cooler without its air getting dirtier.
compare.title: Compare
compare.intro: Up to four designs side by side, with the one we would choose and the reason.
compare.none.name: No trees
compare.none.summary: Open street with no planting. This is the reference the model compares against.
compare.none.reason: The street is open to the wind, so air clears quickly, but the pavement stays hotter.
compare.local.name: Local tree row
compare.local.summary: A typical roadside tree row along the kerb. It adds shade while preserving some ventilation.
compare.local.reason: The crown cools the pavement, but the drag slows the flushing flow enough to matter.
compare.dense.name: Dense tree row
compare.dense.summary: Dense crowns near the walls shorten the opening for the street vortex.
compare.dense.reason: The shade spread is strong, but the airflow is choked and the street keeps more pollution near the pavement.
compare.mixed.name: Trees + hedge
compare.mixed.summary: A hedge can block the most exposed part of the pavement while trees still cool the sunniest zones.
compare.mixed.reason: The hedge modifies the near-wall flow and can improve both outcomes on the right street, which is a real finding rather than a contradiction.
compare.howFrontier: Prefer the design that sits closest to the frontier for the street you actually have.
compare.howBaseline: Only choose a point beyond the baseline if the forecasted heat and fumes both improve.
compare.howReason: Keep the reason short: which design to plant, where it sits in the street, and why it beats the alternatives.
howWeKnow.title: How we know
howWeKnow.intro: The checks behind every number: solver benchmarks, the wind-tunnel reference case, direction checks against published studies, and the AI's accuracy.
leftOut.3d: 3D effects such as junctions, short streets and wind along the street
leftOut.chemistry: NO–NO₂–O₃ chemistry (the fumes are a passive tracer)
leftOut.sway: Crowns that move in the wind (each crown is a fixed porous block)
hongKong.title: Hong Kong
hongKong.intro: Roadside air quality and summer heat stress in Hong Kong, and how the city already assesses air ventilation for large developments.
hongKong.airText: Street-level air pollution is often worse than the general-station background because vehicles release emissions close to people walking at the kerb.
hongKong.heatText: The hottest afternoons are when the sun is low, the street traps the heat, and the pavement stays warm after the air has started to cool.
hongKong.ventText: Hong Kong already checks air ventilation for major developments. This app adds a street-tree check at the scale a community can actually test before planting.
hongKong.atlasText: Three measured streets screened through four fixed planting configurations. Results are simulated; Wing Lok Street is outside the trained aspect-ratio range and must be checked with physics.
report.title: Report
report.intro: A one-page printable summary for a district council or a residents' group.
report.recommendation: {street}: the atlas screens {design} ({status}). Open Design and Trade-off before making a planting decision.
report.noStreet: Choose a street from the Hong Kong atlas, then open this report.
report.evidenceText: The solver is checked against textbook flow cases and CODASC wind-tunnel comparisons. The surrogate metrics below are test-set evidence and remain simulated.
report.whyText: {design} is only a screening recommendation: accept it only after the real physics check and the practical street constraints agree.
report.noChoice: No street recommendation is selected yet.
report.leftOutText: The model leaves out 3D junction effects, chemistry, leaf deposition, evaporation, moving crowns, buoyancy, traffic turbulence and real-scale Reynolds-number effects.
present.title: Presentation mode
present.intro: A full-screen guided story for the four-minute pitch, stepped with the arrow keys or a clicker.
present.slide1.title: Test the change before you plant
present.slide1.body: A tree can cool a narrow street and still make the air at a pedestrian's nose dirtier. This tool tests that trade-off before money, space and materials are committed.
present.slide2.title: Start with the street
present.slide2.body: Choose a measured Hong Kong street or enter a custom cross-section. The practical limits are visible: pavement width, buildings and bus headroom.
present.slide3.title: Change the planting
present.slide3.body: Move and resize tree crowns or add a hedge. The live solver shows wind and fumes while the heat panel reports UTCI on both pavements.
present.slide4.title: Find the trade-off
present.slide4.body: The surrogate sweeps many designs in milliseconds. Cooler designs can carry more fumes, so the frontier makes the choice explicit instead of hiding it.
present.slide5.title: Verify before deciding
present.slide5.body: AI proposes a shortlist. The real solver checks the chosen design, and the evidence screen shows the benchmarks, wind-tunnel comparison and model limits.
present.slide6.title: Choose with the caveats visible
present.slide6.body: Plant the design that fits this street and this decision. Every model number is simulated, and the left-out effects remain visible before anyone treats a screen as a guarantee.

design.aspect: Street shape: building height ÷ street width (H/W)
design.aspectHint: Narrow streets between tall buildings have a high H/W.
design.realUnitsDetail: Approximate lane width {lane} m. The breathing-zone averaging band is {zone} m wide, from {z0} to {z1} m above the ground.
design.expected: What published studies lead us to expect
design.next: Next in phase 3: your own street, and phone mode.
regime.isolatedBody: The buildings are far apart; each disturbs the wind on its own.
regime.wakeBody: The wake behind the upwind building runs into the windward building.
regime.skimmingBody: The wind skims over the roofs and drives one vortex trapped in the street.
regime.deepBody: The trapped air splits into vortices stacked one above the other; the lower one turns slowly.
regime.sourceLiu: Two stacked vortices at H/W 2 in the simulations of Liu, Barth and Leung (2004).
readout.reynoldsHelp: Reynolds number: inflow speed × building height ÷ the model air's viscosity. Real streets have much higher values; this is listed under what the model leaves out.
readout.playbackSlow: This device cannot compute the street at normal speed, so the wind moves more slowly here. The physics and the averages are the same; they take longer to build up.
readout.playbackHelp: Normal speed is the same on every device: the wind above the roofs moves one building height per second. Every device runs the same model on the same grid.
engineNote.noWebgpu: This browser has no WebGPU, so the simulation runs on the CPU: the same model, computed more slowly.
engineNote.webgpuFailed: WebGPU failed to start, so the simulation runs on the CPU: the same model, computed more slowly.
engineNote.gpuLost: The GPU stopped responding, so the simulation moved to the CPU.
evidence.pendingBody: This check has not been run yet. Its result appears here once the pipeline writes it to results/.
hwk.solverIntro: Before the solver is trusted in a street, it has to reproduce flows whose answers are known.
hwk.poisQuestion: Does the solver match the exact profile of flow driven between two plates (Poiseuille)? Target: error below {tol} with {h} cells across or more.
hwk.cavityTitle: Box with a moving lid, Reynolds number {re}
hwk.cavityQuestion: Does the solver reproduce the reference solution of Ghia, Ghia and Shin (1982)? Target: within {tol} of the lid speed.
hwk.cavityChart: Horizontal velocity along the vertical centre line
hwk.massQuestion: In a closed box no air may appear or vanish. Target: change below {tol}.
hwk.lesQuestion: Does the sub-grid model add exactly the eddy viscosity it should (Smagorinsky), with the effect of body forces removed?
hwk.agreeTitle: The same answer on every device
hwk.agreeQuestion: A phone runs the solver on its GPU or CPU; the reference runs in Python. Do they agree? Target: within {tol} of the reference speed.
hwk.agreeJax: The JAX version that runs on the A100 agrees with NumPy to within {worst} of the reference speed.
hwk.streetIntro: The street flow has to show the structures that field studies and other models report.
hwk.regimeTitle: How the air turns as the street narrows
hwk.regimeQuestion: In wide streets the wind reaches the ground; in narrower streets one vortex is trapped; in deep streets vortices stack (Oke 1988; Liu, Barth and Leung 2004). Does the model show this?
hwk.regimeKey: Lines: time-averaged streamlines inside the street, wind from the left. Dots: vortex centres, named from top to bottom.
regimes.plotLabel: Streamlines in a street with H/W {aspect}: {n} stacked vortex cells
hwk.spongeTitle: Sound kept out of the street
hwk.spongeQuestion: Vortices shed by the buildings make sound, which can bounce around the model and drown the real pressure changes. Absorbing layers at the edges should remove it.
hwk.spongeChart: Pressure noise in the street over time
hwk.stabQuestion: Which combinations of Reynolds number and Smagorinsky constant run without blowing up? The live street uses Reynolds number {re} with Cs {cs}.
hwk.later: Checks of the trained fast model (phase 4) are added when it exists.
hwk.check.skimming: Skimming flow: one vortex fills the street (Oke 1988; Liu, Barth and Leung 2004). Vortex cells observed: {n}.
hwk.check.rotation: The vortex turns with the wind above the roofs: clockwise for wind from the left. Observed: {rotation}; top of the street moving at {top} × the inflow speed.
hwk.check.stacked: Vortices stacked one above the other, the upper one turning with the wind above (Liu, Barth and Leung 2004). Observed: {n} stacked cells; top vortex {topRotation}.
hwk.check.wake: The narrower the street, the less of the outer wind reaches into it (Oke 1988). Flow at the top of the street, H/W {aspects}: {tops} × the inflow speed.
hwk.check.deep: Very deep street: vortices stacked one above the other, the upper one turning with the wind above. Observed: {n} stacked cells; top vortex {topRotation}.
hwk.upwindTitle: Why the model street has streets upwind
hwk.upwindQuestion: In a flat (2D) model, the vortex shed by the first building's upwind edge stays over the streets close behind it. Placing the studied street at least three building heights behind the row's edge should give it the skimming flow seen in wind tunnels and city blocks. Does it?
hwk.upwindTop: top of the street ÷ inflow speed
hwk.upwindChart: Time-averaged wind across the middle of the street, H/W 1
hwk.upwindNote: Positive values move with the wind. Under skimming flow the top of the street moves with the wind and the floor against it.
legend.fumes: Fumes, averaged over the last few seconds (c⁺, simulated):
green.title: Greenery
green.light: Light (97.5% open, as CODASC's λ 80 m⁻¹ crown)
green.dense: Dense (96% open, as CODASC's λ 200 m⁻¹ crown)
green.dragHint: You can also drag the greenery sideways in the street.
green.source: Crown shape and density as in the CODASC wind tunnel (Gromke and Ruck); hedge sizes from Gromke et al. (2016). Sizes in metres use this street's buildings, {h} m tall.
exposure.title: Fumes on the pavements
exposure.vsBaseline: {range} against the same street without greenery
exposure.needBaseline: To compare, first run this street without greenery until the averaging finishes.
exposure.baselineReady: This is the street without greenery. Add trees or a hedge to compare with it.
exposure.help: c⁺ is the wind tunnel's normalised concentration: higher means more traffic fumes at breathing height (0.9–2.7 m), within 2.7 m of the wall. A range is the lowest to highest of the last five readings.
exposure.windwardCaveat: In the wind-tunnel comparison the model reads too high at the foot of the windward wall, so treat the right pavement's level with care (How we know).
hwk.greenIntro: Crowns slow the wind and fumes ride on it. Each piece is checked on its own, then the whole street against the CODASC wind tunnel.
hwk.porousQuestion: A porous block across a channel must lose exactly the pressure its drag implies, and give back the pressure-loss coefficient λ the CODASC wind tunnel uses.
hwk.porousBalance: Largest gap in the momentum balance
hwk.porousLambda: λ measured ÷ λ set, dense crown
hwk.porousScaling: Error shrinks when the speed halves
hwk.tracerQuestion: Fumes must not appear or vanish, and a puff must drift and spread as the exact solution says.
hwk.tracerPulse: Largest gap from the exact solution
hwk.codascQuestion: Ten wind-tunnel streets with and without trees (Gromke and Ruck, KIT): does the model's c⁺ on the two walls meet the criteria urban dispersion models are held to (Hanna and Chang 2012)?
hwk.codascOverall: All ten together: FB {fb} (target within ±{fbMax}), NMSE {nmse} (below {nmseMax}), FAC2 {fac2} (above {fac2Min}).
hwk.directionsQuestion: Reviews of street studies find that trees in a narrow street raise the fumes on the pavement, while low hedges lower them; a single hedge in the middle of the road worked best in the wind tunnel (Abhijith et al. 2017). Does the model agree?
hwk.directionsRatio: Leeward pavement {a}, windward pavement {b} against the same street without greenery.
hwk.wallNote: The model follows the leeward wall closely. On the windward wall it holds far too much near the ground: in a 2D model the small eddy in the corner at the foot of the wall is closed, so fumes from the nearest lane escape only slowly. In the wind tunnel, flow along the street probably flushes it.
hwk.reynoldsTitle: Does the answer depend on the model's Reynolds number?
hwk.reynoldsQuestion: Real streets have far higher Reynolds numbers than the model. If pavement exposure hardly moves when the model's Reynolds number doubles, the gap matters less. Target: a change below {tol}.
hwk.reynoldsMiss: Not yet: on this grid the result still moves with the Reynolds number. The same check on the finer grid the GPU engine uses is the next Colab run.
street.drawing: Cross-section to scale, at the median width and height.
street.measured: Measured over {length} m at {used} of {points} points 5 m apart; the rest are junctions and other openings.
street.tooDeep: Deeper than the live model has been checked for (up to H/W {max}); Design shows it at H/W {max}.
street.customText: Set a street width, building height and pavement widths to test a custom cross-section in the live solver.
street.phoneText: Use the compass and tilt sensor for a first-pass street measurement. Enter the distance to the building and a thermometer reading if you have one.
street.phoneDenied: Sensor permission was denied. Enter the bearing and tilt manually instead.
street.phoneCaveat: Height uses h = distance × tan(tilt) + eye height. The interval only represents the angle uncertainty you enter; it is not a survey measurement.

street.later: Your own street, phone mode, the time of day and the weather come later in phase 3.

design.presetScale: Trees and hedges are sized in metres for this street. Traffic lanes and the breathing zone still follow the wind-tunnel street's proportions.
green.sizeLocal: Typical Hong Kong roadside tree: about {h} m tall, crown {s} m across
green.sizeTunnel: As in the wind tunnel: as tall as the buildings
green.sizeLocalNote: Estimated from government tree records near this street: trunk sizes of Highways Department roadside trees, with heights and crowns measured by AFCD on trees of the same trunk size.
street.treesNone: No trees on this stretch in the Highways Department records.
street.treesSome: {n} trees on this stretch in the Highways Department records.
street.treeTypical: A typical roadside tree nearby is about {h} m tall with a crown {s} m across (estimated from government tree records).
recorded.title: Recorded run at the measured shape: {name}, H/W {ratio}
recorded.intro: The live view above cannot take this street's true shape, so it was run once on a finer grid, {h} cells per building height and {w} across the street, and the averages were recorded. Each picture shows the mean fumes in the street and the mean wind around it.
recorded.legend: Mean fumes in the recorded run (c⁺, simulated):
recorded.key: Arrows: mean wind. Dashed boxes: the breathing zone on each pavement. Green: crowns or hedge.
recorded.method: Trees: the typical local roadside tree, {tree} m tall with a {spread} m crown of dense foliage. Hedge: {hh} m high and {hw} m wide. Breathing zone: within {zw} m of each wall, {z0}–{z1} m above the ground. The percentage under a reading compares it with no greenery.
recorded.settlingHelp: "Still moving" is how much the average changed between the first and second half of the recording. A difference between two designs smaller than this is not established.
recorded.source: Recorded on Colab on {date} (commit {commit}). Simulated, not measured.
design.presetRecorded: A run at its measured shape, recorded on a finer grid, is shown below the live view.
hwk.spongeFailedLabel: Step at which the run without the layers failed
heat.directionMeasured: Direction as measured for this street.
heat.weatherSource: Daily values measured at King's Park. The hours in between are rebuilt from them, so read them as typical of that day, not as measurements.
heat.title: Heat on the pavements at {time}
heat.air: Air {t} °C · humidity {rh}% · sunlight {g} W/m² · wind above the roofs {w} m/s
heat.crown: Under the crowns: {p}% of the sun
heat.waiting: Waiting for the wind on the pavements to average…
heat.diagram: The street at {time}: ground in the sun, crowns, people on the pavements and the sun's direction
heat.diagramKey: Thick line: ground in the sun. Arrow: the sun's rays in this cross-section. Upright marks: where the readings are taken.
heat.help: UTCI is a feels-like temperature: the air temperature that would stress the body as much as the real mix of air, sun, wind and humidity. The radiant temperature adds up the sunshine and the heat from sky, walls and ground that reach a person 1.1 m tall.
leftOut.utciWind: Wind in the street is turned into the 10 m wind UTCI expects with an open-country profile, which can misstate UTCI by up to 7 °C in streets (Lee, Park and Mayer 2025)
leftOut.surfaceStorage: Heat stored in walls and paving: surfaces warm and cool at once with the sun
leftOut.clouds: Clouds and haze in the heat radiated by the sky
leftOut.crownDiffuse: Shade from crowns for light from the rest of the sky, and the crowns' own heat
hwk.heatIntro: The sun's position and the heat index are checked against widely used reference libraries.
hwk.sunQuestion: Does our sun position match the NREL algorithm in pvlib, at five latitudes over three years?
hwk.sunElevation: Largest difference in height above the horizon
hwk.utciQuestion: Does our UTCI match pythermalcomfort over the whole range the formula covers?
hwk.collisionTitle: A collision step that holds near its limit
hwk.collisionQuestion: At very low viscosity the standard collision step can blow up. Does the one we use hold where the standard one fails, and does it keep the street calm?
hwk.collisionShear: Runs that stayed stable in a demanding test (standard → ours)
hwk.collisionFlicker: Largest step-to-step flicker in the street, outside the absorbing layers, share of the wind speed (standard → ours)
heat.vsBare: Shade from the greenery: UTCI {d} °C, radiant temperature {r} °C (same wind)
recorded.notSettled: This run had not settled: its averages still moved by up to {p} between the first and second half, more than any design changed them. It shows how the fumes build up in a street this deep in two dimensions, not which design is better.
tradeOff.missing: The AI models are not trained yet. They come from the Colab runs (notebooks 03 and 04); until they are in the app, this screen cannot sweep designs. The live solver on the Design screen works without them.
tradeOff.backend: The AI runs on {backend} in this browser.
tradeOff.failed: The AI models did not load ({message}). The live solver on the Design screen still works.
tradeOff.xLabel: Heat: UTCI on the two pavements, °C
tradeOff.yLabel: Fumes: % of the street without greenery
tradeOff.picksHelp: Three picks from the frontier: the coolest design whose fumes are no worse than the street without greenery, the design with the cleanest air, and the balance point, where the frontier bends most.
tradeOff.noCoolest: No design on the frontier keeps the fumes at or below the street without greenery.
tradeOff.kindRow: One row of trees in the middle
tradeOff.kindRows: Two rows of trees, one near each wall
tradeOff.kindCanopy: Two rows of trees that meet over the street
tradeOff.treeSize: Crowns {z0}–{z1} m above the ground, {w} m wide; foliage λ {lam} per metre
tradeOff.hedgeSize: {h} m high, {w} m wide; foliage λ {lam} per metre
tradeOff.fumes: Fumes against the street without greenery
tradeOff.windValue: {a} and {b} of the wind above the roofs
tradeOff.uncertainty: A range is the spread of five AI models trained separately (two standard deviations each way).
tradeOff.field: Fumes in the street, from the field model
tradeOff.checkHelp: Runs the live solver on this design for as long as each training run ({steps} steps) on this device's processor. It can take several minutes.
tradeOff.checkFilling: The street was still filling with fumes at the end of the run, so the solver's values are low estimates.
tradeOff.checkNoBare: The solver's fumes need the bare street of the same shape from the dataset, which is not in the app yet.
tradeOff.outside: Outside what the AI was trained on — run the physics.
tradeOff.mineOutside: Your design is outside what the AI was trained on — run the physics on the Design screen.
design.toTradeOff: See the trade-off for this street
design.sentLayout: A design from the Trade-off screen. Change any greenery control to go back to your own design.
leftOut.windSpeed: Wind speed in the fumes: the model runs one Reynolds number whatever the wind, and with dense crowns the fumes on the pavements still change with it (How we know)
leftOut.filling: Escape of fumes along the street: in a 2D section a street closed off by dense crowns fills with fumes very slowly, so its readings can still be rising when a run ends
hwk.aiIntro: A surrogate trained on the live solver's own runs answers in milliseconds, so the Trade-off screen can sweep thousands of designs. It is scored against solver runs it never saw.
hwk.aiTitle: How close the AI comes to the solver
hwk.aiQuestion: On designs held back from training, how well does the AI predict the fumes on the pavements that the solver computes?
hwk.aiOod: Streets deeper than the slider allows (out of distribution): R² {r2}, median error {median}, within a factor of two {fac2}. The guard sends {guard} of them to the AI; the rest it refers to the physics.
hwk.aiParity: Pavement fumes c⁺: AI against solver, test designs
